findings.impact_on_revenue: Case-sensitive SQL references or Parquet readers would fail or drop airport fees.
findings.proposed_action: Map canonical 'Airport_fee' -> 'airport_fee' in SQL Builder and Verifier.

findings.baseline_expectation: 19-column 2024 schema (no MTA CBD congestion fee column)
findings.observed_reality: 20-column 2025 schema includes 'cbd_congestion_fee' (non-null in 100.0% of rows, range [0.75, 0.75])
findings.impact_on_revenue: 'cbd_congestion_fee' is included in passenger `total_amount` starting Jan 5, 2025. Omitting it from `surcharges_and_fees_usd` and itemized reconciliation causes component sum to understate `total_amount` by $0.75/trip on CBD rides.
findings.proposed_action: Adapt SQL Builder and Verifier to incorporate COALESCE("cbd_congestion_fee", 0.0) into `surcharges_and_fees_usd` and accounting identity checks.

findings.impact_on_revenue: Cannot attribute revenue to valid finance payment categories.
findings.proposed_action: Refuse to ship summary and escalate unmapped payment_type codes to Finance/Data Eng.

findings.baseline_expectation: Itemized components reconcile with total_amount within $0.05 on >= 95.0% of rows
findings.observed_reality: 4,593 / 12,000 rows (38.27%) fail itemized accounting reconciliation (max discrepancy = $25.00)
findings.impact_on_revenue: total_amount diverges fundamentally from the sum of fare + surcharges + tips + tolls. Shipping either number would report unverified, corrupted revenue to Finance.
findings.proposed_action: Refuse to publish summary and escalate accounting discrepancy to Finance & TLC Vendor Ops.
